body: Paul George picked the right night for his best game in green. In his first trip back to Philadelphia since the July trade that sent him to Boston, he scored 36 points as the Celtics beat the 76ers 123-101 on Nov. 10.
He made 6 of 11 from 3-point range and scored 14 of his points in the fourth quarter.
## Why fans are buying in

The trade is what makes this jersey a story. Boston sent Jaylen Brown, its own 2016 draft pick, to Philadelphia for George plus two first-round and two second-round picks. It was a deal between two rivals, and it put pressure on George to prove the Celtics made the right call.

So far he has. He opened his Boston career with 38 points and seven 3-pointers on Oct. 20, and the win in Philadelphia moved the Celtics to 9-2, the best record in the Eastern Conference. Philadelphia fell to 9-3. Brown finished with 13 points against his old team.

George is also not doing it alone. Jayson Tatum added 21 points, Payton Pritchard had 18, and Boston made 22 of 49 threes as a team. In our analysis, a veteran star who fits right away on a team that is winning is exactly the kind of player new fans rally around. This is our view, not a sales figure.

body: Matthew Golden had his best day as a pro. The Green Bay Packers receiver caught all 10 of his targets for a career-high 164 yards and a touchdown as Green Bay beat the New England Patriots 45-27 at Gillette Stadium on Nov. 8.
He did most of the damage early, with six catches for 126 yards and a score in the first quarter alone.
## Why fans are buying in

That opening quarter put Golden in the Packers' record book. Per the team, it was the most first-quarter receiving yards by a Green Bay receiver since Antonio Freeman had 129 against Tennessee in 1998.

He also shared the spotlight with Christian Watson, who had a career-high 171 yards. They became the first Packers teammates since Don Hutson and Andy Uram in 1942 to each top 150 receiving yards with a touchdown catch in the same game.
The bigger picture is a breakout season. Golden now has 53 catches for 783 yards and five touchdowns through nine games, and the win lifted Green Bay to 6-3.

Golden also carries some history with him. When the Packers took him 23rd overall out of Texas in 2025, he became the team's first first-round receiver since Javon Walker in 2002. In our analysis, a young receiver turning into the go-to target for a winning team is the kind of player a fan base adopts as its own. This is our view, not a sales figure.

title: Cole Hutson's Capitals Jersey Is Rising After His OT Winner
subheadline: The 20-year-old defenseman set up the tying goal and then won it in overtime in Ottawa, with Alex Ovechkin making a little history on the play.
description: Cole Hutson scored 1:14 into overtime as the Capitals beat Ottawa 3-2 on Nov. 10, setting a team record for defensemen. Why his No. 44 Capitals jersey is rising
searchIntent: Capitals and hockey fans who saw Hutson's overtime winner want to know how fast the young defenseman is rising and which Cole Hutson jersey to get.
body: Cole Hutson won it for Washington. The Capitals defenseman scored 1:14 into overtime to beat the Ottawa Senators 3-2 at Canadian Tire Centre on Nov. 10, the first overtime goal of his NHL career.
Earlier he set up Pierre-Luc Dubois for the goal that tied the game 2-2 midway through the third period.
## Why fans are buying in

The winner came on a pass from Alex Ovechkin. That assist was the 762nd of Ovechkin's career, tying Nicklas Backstrom for the most in Capitals history. A young defenseman finishing a play that put the franchise's greatest player into the record book is a moment Washington fans will remember.

Hutson made some team history of his own. The goal and assist gave him 21 points in his first 30 NHL games, and NHL.com notes he is now the fastest defenseman in Capitals history to reach 20 career points, passing a mark of 33 games.

He is still only 20. Washington drafted him in the second round in 2024, and he joined the team late last season after starring at Boston University, where he had 32 points in 35 games. The win moved the Capitals to 10-6-0 and gave them two straight after they trailed 2-1 going into the third period.

In our analysis, a puck-moving defenseman who produces offense this early is the kind of player fans pick as the next face of a team, especially with Ovechkin near the end of his career. This is our view, not a sales figure.
## The look
Hutson wears No. 44. The banner above shows the red Capitals home jersey, the look that fills the arena on game nights in Washington.
